dogWalksAway.guidance: Make the session easier. Move to a quieter space and reward one second of attention before asking for the full behavior.

dogJumpsForTreat.prompt: My dog jumps for the treat
dogJumpsForTreat.guidance: Hold the treat closer to their nose and move it more slowly, so jumping is never rewarded.

dogDistracted.guidance: Move somewhere quieter with fewer sounds and smells, then try again.

dogDoesntUnderstand.guidance: Break the behavior into a smaller step and reward that smaller step for a few reps first.

dogGetsFrustrated.guidance: Shorten the session and end on an easy win. Frustration usually means the ask is too big right now.

dogAlreadyKnowsThis.guidance: Great — add a small distraction or distance to keep it interesting, or move ahead to the next lesson.

bitingFrustrated.guidance: Pause and offer a chew toy instead of a hand or sleeve. Frustration during mouthing games often means it's time for a break.

bitingCausesInjury.guidance: This goes beyond what in-app guidance can safely cover. Please consult a certified professional dog trainer or your veterinarian.
